Definition: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (ὄνομαι, to slur); for which another prolonged form (ὀνάω) is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of G3686 through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from:--have joy.
BiblicalUsage: Oninemi means to profit, to have joy of someone, to be refreshed by them. It occurs once, in Philemon 1:20, where Paul asks, let me have joy of thee in the Lord, refresh my bowels in the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's joy in Philemon is the profit of the gospel, and a brother refreshed is a brother gained.
